beats.label: S1 · Secret therapy
beats.text: Panic attacks send New Jersey capo Tony Soprano into secret therapy with Dr. Melfi, where he unpacks his fear of losing his family and hatred of his mother Livia.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the show's core premise and every season's central relationship.

beats.label: S1 · Junior as figurehead
beats.text: When acting boss Jackie Aprile dies of cancer, Tony backs his volatile uncle Junior as the new boss so Junior can wear the crown while Tony truly runs the crew.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up the power arrangement whose collapse drives the season's plot.

beats.label: S1 · Livia in the home
beats.text: Tony forces a resistant Livia into a nursing home; riding with Junior to Tony's house, Junior muses that 'something may have to be done' about him, and Livia quietly smiles.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The whispered instigation that sets the season's hit in motion.

beats.label: S1 · Pussy vanishes
beats.text: Pussy Bonpensiero vanishes under suspicion of wearing a wire, leaving Tony grief-stricken and paranoid about who else around him may have flipped.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Plants the informant thread that defines S2.

beats.label: S1 · Failed hit
beats.text: Junior's hitmen ambush Tony but botch the job — one shoots the other by mistake — and Livia, visiting his hospital room, feigns memory loss to cover her role.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Tony now knows, in his bones, that his own mother wants him dead.

beats.label: S1 · Livia exposed
beats.text: FBI tapes catch Livia goading Junior into the hit; Tony rushes to smother her in bed but staff wheel her out first as she suffers a timely stroke. Junior is arrested.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Removes Junior from play and leaves Livia neutralised but alive.

beats.label: S1 · Vesuvio in the storm
beats.text: A blackout drives the family to Artie's rebuilt Vesuvio, where Tony tells his children to 'remember the little moments that were good.'
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's emotional exhale — Tony has kept his family and the tone he wants to be leaving them with.

cliffhanger.text: Tony has survived a hit ordered by his own mother, but she has slipped consequences behind a convenient stroke and Junior sits in a jail cell refusing to flip. Pussy is still missing, and Melfi is in hiding.
questions: Will Junior break under federal pressure and give Tony up?
Is Pussy dead, running, or somewhere wearing a wire?
How much of Livia's manipulation did the FBI tapes actually capture?

characters.name: Tony Soprano
characters.line: A New Jersey DiMeo capo in secret therapy, who has just discovered his own mother helped orchestrate a hit on him.

characters.name: Carmela Soprano
characters.line: Tony's Catholic wife, aware of the mob work but insulated from it, and suspicious of the female therapist she has never met.

characters.name: Livia Soprano
characters.line: Tony's malevolent mother, hiding behind a stroke and feigned dementia after her plot was uncovered.

characters.name: Corrado 'Junior' Soprano
characters.line: Tony's uncle, technically boss of the family, freshly arrested on federal charges and so far refusing to inform.

characters.name: Dr. Jennifer Melfi
characters.line: Tony's psychiatrist, forced into hiding after his enemies made her a possible target.

characters.name: Christopher Moltisanti
characters.line: Tony's ambitious young protégé and cousin by marriage, dating Adriana La Cerva.

characters.name: Salvatore 'Big Pussy' Bonpensiero
characters.line: Longtime crew member who has vanished, suspected of wearing an FBI wire.

characters.name: Meadow Soprano
characters.line: Tony's teenage daughter, who now knows exactly what her father actually does for a living.

beats.label: S2 · Pussy resurfaces
beats.text: Four months on, Pussy returns claiming a bad-back sabbatical; Tony pretends to believe him while quietly wondering when the FBI turned his oldest friend.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The informant clock that will run all season starts here.

beats.label: S2 · Richie paroled
beats.text: Jackie Aprile's older brother Richie is released after ten years, refuses to defer to Tony, and takes up a violent affair with Tony's sister Janice.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the season's chief internal antagonist and Janice as a wild card.

beats.label: S2 · Furio arrives
beats.text: Tony brings Neapolitan enforcer Furio Giunta back to New Jersey and promotes Silvio and Paulie past Pussy, feeding Pussy's grievance and deepening his cooperation.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Furio's arrival and Pussy's snub both feed into the season's endgame.

beats.label: S2 · Pussy confirmed
beats.text: Pussy, wired for the FBI, murders an associate who spotted him with his handler and reports on Tony's confirmation dinner from inside the family's own home.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Shifts Pussy from suspect to certain rat in the viewer's mind.

beats.label: S2 · Janice shoots Richie
beats.text: Richie asks a capo to sanction a hit on Tony; Junior rats him out, but before Tony can act, Janice shoots Richie dead in her kitchen over dinner.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Removes Richie and quietly deepens the debt Tony owes Junior.

beats.label: S2 · Pussy at sea
beats.text: A fever dream tells Tony what he already knows. He finds Pussy's wire, takes him on the boat with Silvio and Paulie, and executes him over the Atlantic.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's central betrayal is settled — cleanly for Tony, unforgettably for his crew.

beats.label: S2 · Livia on the tarmac
beats.text: Livia is caught trying to flee the country on stolen airline tickets Tony gave her; the FBI briefly arrests Tony, and Melfi presses him on the connection.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Livia is still in play, and Melfi's re-commitment lets therapy stay the show's engine.

cliffhanger.text: Pussy and Richie are gone and Tony's crew is smaller and tighter, but the FBI walked out of the airport with Livia and Melfi still cannot say why she keeps taking Tony's money.
questions: What did Livia tell the Feds when they had her alone?
Will Junior stay loyal from prison, or is his patience running out?
How long can Chris survive being both Tony's heir and lowest earner?

characters.name: Tony Soprano
characters.line: DiMeo capo, unchallenged inside his own crew after Pussy and Richie have both been dealt with.

characters.name: Carmela Soprano
characters.line: Tony's wife, feeling him drift and increasingly resentful of the infidelities she has stopped bothering to hide from herself.

characters.name: Livia Soprano
characters.line: Tony's mother, arrested at the airport with the stolen tickets he gave her, still alive and still trouble.

characters.name: Junior Soprano
characters.line: On house arrest awaiting trial and freshly, warily reconciled with Tony after ratting out Richie.

characters.name: Dr. Jennifer Melfi
characters.line: Tony's psychiatrist, back treating him despite her own analyst's warnings about her thrill in the room.

characters.name: Christopher Moltisanti
characters.line: Tony's protégé, having burned his Hollywood ambitions to stay in the family.

characters.name: Furio Giunta
characters.line: Newly imported Neapolitan enforcer, quickly Tony's favourite piece of muscle.

characters.name: Silvio Dante
characters.line: Tony's consigliere and operator of the Bada Bing strip club.

characters.name: Paulie Gualtieri
characters.line: Longtime soldier freshly promoted past Pussy, superstitious and easily wounded.

beats.label: S3 · Livia dies
beats.text: Livia dies of a stroke early in the season, freeing Tony from his lifelong tormentor and setting his sister Janice fighting over the family house.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Removes the show's original antagonist and leaves Tony to work out what she meant to him.

beats.label: S3 · Ralphie rises
beats.text: Sadistic soldier Ralphie Cifaretto pushes hard for capo, beats a young Bada Bing stripper to death, and takes up with Jackie Aprile's widow Rosalie.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the man Tony will spend two seasons unable to stomach or dismiss.

beats.label: S3 · Melfi's silence
beats.text: Melfi is raped and her attacker walks free on a technicality; she does not give Tony the man's name, though the temptation to loose him nearly breaks her.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's clearest look at what Melfi has been holding back from her own patient.

beats.label: S3 · Gloria and violence
beats.text: Tony begins a volatile affair with car dealer Gloria Trillo — another Melfi patient — that ends with him nearly strangling her when she threatens to tell Carmela.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Reveals how dangerous Tony has become to the women who resemble his mother.

beats.label: S3 · Jackie Jr. and Meadow
beats.text: Meadow dates the Aprile heir Jackie Jr., whom Tony repeatedly warns off the mob life; Jackie flunks out of college and drifts toward gangster fantasies anyway.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Puts a Soprano child inside the exact story Tony has tried to keep her out of.

beats.label: S3 · Jackie's execution
beats.text: Jackie robs a made card game and gets his friends killed; Tony leaves the decision to Ralphie, who has Vito execute him and dresses it as a drug deal.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Ralphie's first big kill on Tony's watch and the trigger for Meadow's disillusionment.

beats.label: S3 · Meadow walks out
beats.text: At Jackie's wake a drunk, grieving Meadow decries the whole scene as 'bullshit' and runs off; Tony reluctantly promotes Ralphie as the only man qualified for capo.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Both endings of the season — the daughter he has lost and the man he cannot get rid of.

cliffhanger.text: Ralphie has the capo seat Tony wanted to keep from him, Meadow is quietly done with what her father does, and an undercover FBI agent has just become Adriana's best friend.
questions: How long can Tony work with a capo he actively loathes?
Will Adriana's new friend get her to say something she cannot take back?
What does Carmela do with the feelings she has quietly developed for Furio?

characters.name: Tony Soprano
characters.line: DiMeo acting boss whose mother is finally dead, whose daughter has quietly turned on him, and whose newest capo he cannot stand.

characters.name: Carmela Soprano
characters.line: Tony's wife, increasingly tired of the excuses she makes for the marriage.

characters.name: Meadow Soprano
characters.line: At Columbia and freshly disillusioned with her father after his world got Jackie Jr. killed.

characters.name: A.J. Soprano
characters.line: Tony's teenage son, having his first panic attacks.

characters.name: Dr. Jennifer Melfi
characters.line: Tony's psychiatrist, carrying the secret of her own rape and choosing, at real cost, not to tell him.

characters.name: Christopher Moltisanti
characters.line: Made man, engaged to Adriana, resentful of still having to kick up to Paulie.

characters.name: Adriana La Cerva
characters.line: Chris's fiancée and the Crazy Horse's manager, being cultivated by an undercover FBI agent she has no idea is a plant.

characters.name: Ralphie Cifaretto
characters.line: Vicious new capo, dating Rosalie Aprile, promoted only because Tony had no one else.

characters.name: Junior Soprano
characters.line: On house arrest with newly diagnosed stomach cancer, still mentally sharp.

characters.name: Furio Giunta
characters.line: Tony's Neapolitan enforcer.

beats.label: S4 · Adriana wired
beats.text: Fresh from being made, Chris slips back onto heroin while Adriana, cornered by FBI agents at last, starts leaking scraps of information to buy time.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The informant thread that shapes every future season starts here in earnest.

beats.label: S4 · Ralphie's joke
beats.text: Ralphie insults Johnny Sac's wife Ginny's weight; the joke leaks and escalates into simmering hostility between the DiMeo family and the New York Lupertazzis.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up the war footing between Tony and New York that will run for years.

beats.label: S4 · Furio and Carmela
beats.text: Furio returns from his father's funeral quietly in love with Carmela; the two ache toward an affair that never quite happens before he flees to Italy without warning.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The love story that finally breaks Carmela's tolerance for the marriage.

beats.label: S4 · Ralphie strangled
beats.text: A stable fire kills Tony's beloved racehorse Pie-O-My. Convinced Ralphie set it for the insurance, Tony strangles him in his own kitchen; he and Chris dispose of the body.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Removes Ralphie in the season's most privately felt murder and further isolates Tony.

beats.label: S4 · Chris in rehab
beats.text: After Chris kills Adriana's dog while high and hits her, Tony stages an intervention that turns into a beating and sends Chris to rehab — buying Adriana time to keep her secret.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Keeps Chris and Adriana both alive going into the next season's collision.

beats.label: S4 · Junior's mistrial
beats.text: A bribed juror hangs Junior's jury and his RICO case is declared a mistrial; Tony's crew tightens as his marriage frays under his infidelities and Carmela's private ache for Furio.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Junior stays free just as the household falls apart.

beats.label: S4 · Carmela throws Tony out
beats.text: Irina calls the house in spite and tells Carmela about Tony sleeping with Svetlana; Carmela ends the marriage and refuses to yield when Tony begs.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The rupture that defines the show going forward.

cliffhanger.text: Tony is living alone in his dead mother's house, his marriage in ruins over infidelities Carmela will no longer overlook, and Adriana is trapped between the Bureau and the boy she is about to marry.
questions: Will Tony and Carmela ever reconcile?
How long can Adriana keep her cooperation hidden from Chris?
Does the truce with New York survive its next real test?

characters.name: Tony Soprano
characters.line: DiMeo capo, thrown out by Carmela and back living in Livia's old house after strangling Ralphie.

characters.name: Carmela Soprano
characters.line: Estranged from Tony and out for a fair share of assets the law will not let her touch, still privately mourning Furio.

characters.name: Meadow Soprano
characters.line: At Columbia, back at school after a shaky stretch following Jackie Jr.'s murder.

characters.name: A.J. Soprano
characters.line: Teenage son, drifting, resistant to any kind of shaping.

characters.name: Dr. Jennifer Melfi
characters.line: Still Tony's psychiatrist, watching him unravel through the separation.

characters.name: Christopher Moltisanti
characters.line: Made man, freshly out of rehab and sober, engaged to Adriana.

characters.name: Adriana La Cerva
characters.line: Chris's fiancée, FBI informant now leaking real information under the threat of prosecution.

characters.name: Junior Soprano
characters.line: Beat the RICO case with a mistrial and remains on the outside.

characters.name: Johnny Sacrimoni
characters.line: Underboss of the New York Lupertazzi family, quietly at war with Tony over Ralphie's joke and being cut out of the mortgage scheme.

beats.label: S5 · Class of '04
beats.text: Ten months on, four mob veterans are paroled at once — among them Tony's cousin Tony Blundetto, who insists he only wants to go straight as a massage therapist.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces Blundetto, the season's tragic engine, and the wave of newly-freed old-timers.

beats.label: S5 · Carmine dies
beats.text: Lupertazzi boss Carmine has a fatal stroke; his son Little Carmine and underboss Johnny Sac split the family, and newly-freed capo Phil Leotardo goes to war for Johnny.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The New York succession fight that becomes the season's political spine.

beats.label: S5 · Adriana confesses
beats.text: A body dumped at Adriana's club forces her hand with her FBI handlers, and after weeks of terror she confesses everything to Chris in a diner parking lot.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The reveal that turns Chris's marriage into a life-or-death decision.

beats.label: S5 · Adriana in the woods
beats.text: Chris briefly considers running with Adriana, then sells her out; Silvio drives her into the woods on the pretext of a hospital visit and shoots her while she begs.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The murder that will define Chris for the rest of the show.

beats.label: S5 · Blundetto's war
beats.text: Blundetto takes a paid hit on Phil's man Joey Peeps and later kills Phil's brother Billy; Tony refuses to give his cousin up despite New York's fury.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Puts Phil Leotardo on the road to a personal vendetta that outlasts every truce.

beats.label: S5 · Tony kills Tony
beats.text: Melfi and Silvio both tell Tony he is shielding Blundetto out of guilt for the panic attack that spared him from prison; Tony finds him at their uncle's farm and shoots him dead himself.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Denies Phil his torture and closes the season on Tony's most personal killing.

beats.label: S5 · Snow at Johnny's
beats.text: Tony reconciles with Carmela and offers Blundetto's body to Johnny Sac, only for the FBI to raid the summit; Tony ditches his gun and flees home through the snow.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Marriage restored, but the season ends with Tony on the run and Phil unappeased.

cliffhanger.text: Tony is home and back with Carmela, but Phil Leotardo has a killed brother to answer for, Adriana is missing without explanation, and the Feds just watched Tony run from a Mafia summit.
questions: Will Phil accept his brother's killer being already dead?
How long until someone realises Adriana is not on holiday?
Can Chris live with what he did, sober?

characters.name: Tony Soprano
characters.line: DiMeo boss, back home with Carmela but exposed to New York and to the FBI at once.

characters.name: Carmela Soprano
characters.line: Reconciled with Tony after a year of separation, having failed to secure independence on her own terms.

characters.name: Meadow Soprano
characters.line: Engaged to Finn DeTrolio and thinking about law school.

characters.name: A.J. Soprano
characters.line: Drifting through nightclubs and part-time work with no discernible direction.

characters.name: Dr. Jennifer Melfi
characters.line: Still treating Tony and still rebuffing his advances on the couch.

characters.name: Christopher Moltisanti
characters.line: Made man and freshly widowed of the fiancée he sold out to Silvio's gun.

characters.name: Junior Soprano
characters.line: In steep cognitive decline, suffering infarcts and taunting Tony that he 'never had the makings of a varsity athlete.'

characters.name: Silvio Dante
characters.line: Tony's consigliere, and the man who put Adriana in the ground.

characters.name: Johnny Sacrimoni
characters.line: Boss of the Lupertazzi family, just arrested by the FBI mid-summit with Tony.

characters.name: Phil Leotardo
characters.line: Newly-paroled Lupertazzi capo whose brother was killed by Blundetto and whose grief has curdled into a personal war.

beats.label: S6 · Junior shoots Tony
beats.text: Junior, deep in dementia, mistakes Tony for a long-dead enemy and shoots him in the stomach; Tony spends weeks in a coma dreaming as salesman 'Kevin Finnerty.'
beats.whyLoadBearing: The event that reorders the crew, the family, and Tony's own head.

beats.label: S6 · Vito outed
beats.text: Tony wakes vowing to see every day as a gift, but his crew reads the softness; when capo Vito Spatafore is spotted in a gay club, he flees to a small town in New Hampshire.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The prejudice storyline that reveals where Tony's leadership has actually landed.

beats.label: S6 · Vito killed
beats.text: Vito's small-town idyll fails and he returns to New Jersey; Phil Leotardo, now boss after Johnny Sac takes a plea, has him beaten to death with pool cues.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The killing that puts Phil and Tony openly on a collision course.

beats.label: S6 · Cleaver
beats.text: Chris directs a mob slasher, Cleaver, whose villain is transparently Tony; Tony reads it as Chris finally admitting the hate he still carries over Adriana.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The rupture between Tony and his supposed heir made unmistakable, on film.

beats.label: S6 · Chris murdered
beats.text: Chris crashes his SUV while high with Tony as passenger; injured and afraid a drug test will finish him, he lets Tony finish him first, by hand.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Removes Tony's protégé and closes the loop that started when Chris chose the mob.

beats.label: S6 · Phil rejects peace
beats.text: Phil turns on Tony over asbestos dumping and refuses every peace offering; Tony, tipped off by the FBI in exchange for Muslim contacts at the Bing, pre-empts the war.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The moment the whole show reduces to two men trying to kill each other first.

beats.label: S6 · Diner
beats.text: Bobby is shot dead, Silvio is left comatose, Phil is killed at a gas station; Tony sits with his family in Holsten's diner as a stranger enters, and the shot cuts to black.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The show's final image and every question it refuses to answer.

cliffhanger.text: The war with New York is won at devastating cost — Bobby dead, Silvio in a coma, capo Carlo flipped to the Feds — and Tony sits with Carmela, Meadow and A.J. in a diner as a stranger walks past to the men's room and the screen cuts to black.
questions: Does the man in the diner mean Tony harm, or does he mean nothing at all?
Will Carlo's testimony put Tony away?
What is left of the crew Tony still commands?

characters.name: Tony Soprano
characters.line: DiMeo boss, survivor of Junior's bullet, murderer of his own protégé, and the last man standing at the end of a two-family war.

characters.name: Carmela Soprano
characters.line: Reconciled with Tony, complicit in the money without ever quite touching the blood.

characters.name: Meadow Soprano
characters.line: Engaged to Patsy's son Patrick and committed to becoming a white-collar defence lawyer.

characters.name: A.J. Soprano
characters.line: Recovering from a suicide attempt in his own pool, unstable, being set up with a Little Carmine production job.

characters.name: Dr. Jennifer Melfi
characters.line: Tony's ex-psychiatrist, having dropped him after reading that sociopaths use therapy as a workshop.

characters.name: Christopher Moltisanti
characters.line: Tony's protégé, murdered by Tony's own hand after the car crash exposed his relapse.

characters.name: Junior Soprano
characters.line: In a state psychiatric facility, no longer recognising Tony at all.

characters.name: Paulie Gualtieri
characters.line: Reluctantly promoted to capo of the Aprile Crew after Carlo Gervasi vanished into federal custody.

characters.name: Silvio Dante
characters.line: Tony's consigliere, left in a coma after Phil's ambush and unlikely to wake.

characters.name: Bobby Baccalieri
characters.line: Janice's husband and Tony's brother-in-law, shot dead by Phil's hitmen in a train hobby shop.

characters.name: Phil Leotardo
characters.line: Lupertazzi boss who ordered the hits on Tony's crew and was killed at a Long Island gas station in return.
